benefits: Performance-based scholarships awarded under Section 57 of the Austrian Student Support Act (StudFG) to recognise exceptional academic performance
Scholarships for scientific theses supporting unfinished scientific work
Application through the LFU:online student platform
eligibility: Performance-based scholarships: Austrian citizens, citizens from EEA states and stateless persons granted equal status
Admission to or enrolment in a degree programme at the University of Innsbruck
Grade point average no lower than 2.0 for the examinations, courses and written pieces submitted
A minimum number of semester hours/ECTS credits completed in the year prior to the application, set per faculty
requirements: Grade point average of at least 2.0 for the submitted examinations and work
Faculty-specific ECTS minimums and maximum grade thresholds for the academic year prior to the application
documents: Application form for the respective scholarship
For scholarships for scientific theses: overview of costs, description of the written thesis, financing plan and expert opinion of the thesis supervisor

applicant_utility.summary: Innsbruck runs two StudFG schemes: performance-based scholarships (Section 57) for a GPA of at least 2.0 with faculty-specific ECTS and grade thresholds, and scholarships for scientific theses that require a cost overview and financing plan. Both go through LFU:online; the published page still shows the 2023/24 call (2 September - 4 October 2024), so check for the current window before applying.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Austrian and EEA nationals (and equal-status stateless persons) with consistently strong grades, or thesis-stage students who can document thesis-related costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Check that your GPA on the exams you submit is at least 2.0 and inside your faculty's grade threshold
Confirm the ECTS minimum for the prior year in your faculty's rules - it differs by faculty
Prepare the thesis-scholarship pack: cost overview, thesis description, financing plan and supervisor opinion
Watch the scholarships page for the current call - the visible one is still 2023/24
common_rejection_risks: Applying as a third-country national - these schemes cover Austrian, EEA and equal-status stateless persons
Exceeding the maximum study period for performance scholarships (Section 18 StudFG) without a documented reason
Counting the dissertation inside the ECTS, which the rules exclude
Submitting outside LFU:online without first contacting the College Service Center
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs and tuition; the thesis scholarship covers defined thesis costs, not general living expenses.
document_audit: Thesis scholarships require the supervisor's expert opinion on the correct faculty-specific form
Only exams completed between 1 October and 30 September of the relevant window count towards the application
alerts: The visible call is for academic year 2023/24 - the current cycle may have different dates
Joint study programmes with UMIT must be filed at the University of Innsbruck
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Verify GPA and ECTS thresholds -> apply via LFU:online in the call window -> College Service Center processes -> decision by the responsible working groups.
